question:
For $-1
(a) Explain why the stated interval is an admissible domain for both $P$ and $Q$.

(b) Establish a relation between $P(x)$ and $Q(x)$.

(c) Evaluate $Q\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)$ using the established relation.

(d) Solve $Q(x)=\frac{\pi}{6}$ and verify that the solution belongs to the stated domain.
explanation:
(a)
For $-10$, so $\sqrt{1-x^2}$ is real and positive. Therefore, $\frac{x}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}$ is a real number and belongs to the domain of $\tan^{-1}x$. Thus, both expressions are defined on $(-1,1)$.

(b)
Let $P(x)=\theta$. Then $$\theta=\sin^{-1}x,\qquad -\frac{\pi}{2}<\theta<\frac{\pi}{2}$$ Therefore, $x=\sin\theta$. Since $\cos\theta>0$ in this interval, $$\sqrt{1-x^2}=\sqrt{1-\sin^2\theta}=\cos\theta$$ Hence, $$\frac{x}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}=\frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}=\tan\theta$$ Since $\theta$ lies in the principal range of inverse tangent, $$Q(x)=\tan^{-1}(\tan\theta)=\theta=P(x)$$ Thus, $Q(x)=\sin^{-1}x$.

(c)
Using the established relation, $$Q\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)=\sin^{-1}\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)=-\frac{\pi}{6}$$

(d)
Since $Q(x)=\sin^{-1}x$, the equation becomes $$\sin^{-1}x=\frac{\pi}{6}$$ Taking sine gives $$x=\sin\frac{\pi}{6}=\frac{1}{2}$$ Since $-1<\frac{1}{2}<1$, the solution belongs to the domain. Therefore, $x=\frac{1}{2}$.

options.A:
(a) Both functions are defined on $(-1,1)$ because $1-x^2>0$ and the denominator is non-zero

(b) $Q(x)=P(x)=\sin^{-1}x$

(c) $Q\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right)=-\dfrac{\pi}{6}$

(d) $x=\dfrac{1}{2}$, which belongs to $(-1,1)$
options.B:
(a) Both functions are defined on $[-1,1]$ because the denominator may equal zero at the endpoints

(b) $Q(x)=-P(x)$

(c) $Q\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right)=\dfrac{\pi}{6}$

(d) $x=-\dfrac{1}{2}$
options.C:
(a) Both functions are defined only on $(0,1)$ because the square root must be positive

(b) $Q(x)=\dfrac{\pi}{2}-P(x)$

(c) $Q\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right)=\dfrac{2\pi}{3}$

(d) $x=\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$
options.D:
(a) Both functions are defined for every real $x$

(b) $Q(x)=2P(x)$

(c) $Q\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right)=-\dfrac{\pi}{3}$

(d) $x=\sin\dfrac{\pi}{12}$
